headline: Max Verstappen climbed from fifth to win a red-flag-interrupted Mexico City Grand Prix, holding off pole-sitter Lewis Hamilton by eight-tenths of a second.
whatHappened: Lewis Hamilton led early from pole position, but a mid-race red flag for a multi-car crash disrupted Ferrari's planned one-stop strategy. Max Verstappen used an aggressive undercut strategy prior to the stoppage to gain track position over the front row starters. After the standing restart, Verstappen managed high brake and engine temperatures in Mexico City's thin air while fending off a late charge from Hamilton. Kimi Antonelli avoided the chaos to bring his Mercedes home third, securing vital points while five drivers retired.
keyBattle: The winning move happened in the pit lane on lap 42 when Red Bull called Verstappen in for hard tyres just as a Virtual Safety Car was deployed for Bottas's stalled car. Ferrari kept Hamilton out for one lap too long, costing him three seconds of track position and handing Verstappen the lead he would keep to the finish.
championshipImpact: Antonelli's third-place finish extended his championship lead to 119 points over Verstappen with three races remaining. Verstappen moved past Hamilton into second in the drivers' standings by two points, while McLaren's lower-points finish effectively ended Norris's mathematical title hopes.
watchThis: Observe how drivers lift and coast several hundred meters before the heavy braking zone at Turn 1 to keep engine and brake temperatures within safe limits at 2,200 meters above sea level. Notice how Verstappen minimised steering lock through the slow stadium section to protect his worn front-left tyre from excessive graining.
